correctness_confidence.basis: Complete machine-checked proof in Lean 4.35.0 with zero sorry, zero warnings, and zero Classical.choice across 18 theorems, complemented by a zero-floating-point discrete Python verifier rejecting 60/60 adversarial forgeries.

novelty.basis: First formal verification of Escardó and Oliva's recent (Nov 2026) monadic continuation formulation of alpha-beta pruning and optimal-play extraction.

reproducibility.basis: Standalone zero-dependency Lean 4 module, 16 canonical certificates, and automated red-team test suite providing deterministic local verification across all tracked artifacts.

rigor.basis: Exhaustive formalization of reader/continuation monads, takeUntil short-circuiting, Lemma 2 soundness, Theorem 1, Corollaries 1(a)-(b) and 2, tie-preserving pickMax/pickMin, and history-dependent Tic-Tac-Toe search.

significance.basis: Bridges abstract denotational semantics of sequential games with practical alpha-beta search and rigorous discrete certificate validation, establishing absolute correctness guarantees for game trees.

strengths: Zero-sorry, zero-Classical.choice formalization of 18 core theorems in Lean 4.35.0.
Robust discrete Python verifier (ALPHABETA-MONAD-CERT-1.0) enforcing strict JSON typing and bounds.
Comprehensive red-team suite successfully rejecting 60/60 forged payloads.
Scales cleanly to history-dependent Tic-Tac-Toe (362,880 to 9,335 evaluated plays).
strong_novelty_candidates: First machine-checked formalization of monadic continuation alpha-beta pruning with history-dependent games and tie-breaking guarantees.
summary: The manuscript presents a rigorous, machine-checked verification framework for Escardó and Oliva's monadic continuation alpha-beta pruning theory. With 18 zero-sorry Lean 4 theorems, a zero-floating-point discrete verifier, canonical certificates, and a 60/60 adversarial red-team suite, the work achieves exemplary formal standards and complete correctness.
weaknesses: Scope is tightly focused on discrete integer payoffs and specific game trees, leaving broader continuous game domains for future work.
